newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon increases tax on luxury cars imports.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon increases tax on luxury cars imports.

text.p: Lebanon's cabinet decided in a late night extraordinary meeting to increase customs tax on luxury cars by up to 200 percent.
"The cabinet decided a minimum customs tax (on cars) of five million Lebanese pounds ($3,245)," Acting Finance Minister Fuoad Siniora was quoted on Wednesday as saying.

He said the new tax will be: "20 percent on cars worth 15 million pounds, 50 percent on cars worth between 15 million pounds and 50 million, 100 percent on cars worth between 50 million pounds and 100 million and 200 percent on cars worth more than 100 million pounds".
Siniora said this decision will have positive effect on the enviromental situation, the number of cars in the country and the balance of payments.
Lebanon's balance of payments registered a surplus of $500 million at the end of April, according to Bank of Lebanon figures.
"Lebanon's annual imported car bill is $800 million ... We import 75,000 car a year and we have now about 1,300,000 cars which means a car for each three citizens," Siniora said.
